title.narrative: Activity under preparation Strategic Communication and Public Diplomacy ¿ Global Gateway Colombia

description.narrative: The proposed action supports the shift from partner-implemented, project-based communication towards a Delegation-led, strategic and political communication approach, fully in line with the Cooperation Facility Guidelines 2023. The intervention will be grounded in a clear brand-building purpose, aimed at positioning the European Union as a visible, credible and values-based global actor in Colombia. In this context, brand building is understood not as promotional activity, but as the deliberate construction of a coherent political identity and narrative that conveys the EU¿s role, added value and long-term commitment as a global partner for peace, democracy, trade, human rights, investments and inclusion. This approach implies moving beyond the aggregation of individual projects or isolated success stories towards a clear, consistent and recognisable narrative that links EU political priorities, strategic investments and values under the Global Gateway umbrella. By strengthening message coherence and continuity over time, the action will enhance the EU¿s visibility and differentiation as a global actor, contribute to shaping public perceptions and support the EU¿s broader political and economic objectives in Colombia. The intervention strategy is designed as a large-scale, multi-year 360° communication campaign, combining digital outreach, media partnerships, influencer engagement, audiovisual storytelling and targeted public diplomacy actions. These actions will be designed to engage political, institutional, academic, media and opinion-shaping stakeholders, providing platforms for dialogue, visibility and positioning of the EU on strategic issues linked to Global Gateway. By complementing mass communication with direct engagement and high-level visibility initiatives, public diplomacy will reinforce the EU¿s profile as a relevant political and strategic actor, enhance its ability to shape narratives and contribute to strengthening relationships with key interlocutors in Colombia.The campaign will also prioritise outreach to new and non-traditional audiences, in particular young people aged 18¿35, mostly located in urban areas, using short-form content, social media, digital platforms and trusted voices. Message coherence across sectors will be ensured through a unified narrative framework, strengthening the EU¿s political positioning as a long-term, values-based partner.
